title: The Shape-Shifting NOT
kidRule: IN at the front of a word can mean 'not'. It is a shape-shifter that changes to match the next letter: IM before M, P or B, IL before L, and IR before R. Then keep every letter of the whole word, so im + mature has two M's and il + legal has two L's.
hint: This word is a little 'not' beginning stuck onto a whole word. Which letter does the whole word start with? That tells you whether the beginning is I-N, I-M, I-L or I-R.
reminder: The 'not' beginning matches the next letter: I-M before M, P or B, I-L before L, I-R before R. Then keep the whole word, so a letter may come twice.

check.question: Why does IMPOSSIBLE begin with I-M and not I-N?
check.correctAnswer: The 'not' beginning IN changes to IM before a P, and POSSIBLE keeps every letter!
distractors: Because I-N is never allowed at the start of a long word
Because POSSIBLE loses its P and the M takes its place

words.why: I-N joins CORRECT, so there is one N and two R's.
words.sent: One answer on my math page was incorrect.
words.story: People once thought that the sun went around the Earth. That idea was incorrect: the Earth goes around the sun!
words.card: Is it *correct* to wear socks on your ears? No, that is *incorrect*!

words.why: I-M joins POSSIBLE, because IN changes to IM before P.
words.def: Not able to happen or be done.
words.sent: It is impossible to count every star in the sky.
words.story: Many people once said it was impossible for humans to fly. Then, in 1903, the Wright brothers flew the first airplane!
words.card: It is *possible* to hug a pillow, but *impossible* to hug a cloud!

words.why: I-N joins COMPLETE, with no letters lost.
words.def: Not finished; with a part missing.
words.sent: The puzzle was incomplete because one piece was lost.
words.story: Our maps of the deep ocean floor are still incomplete, because most of it has never been mapped in detail!
words.card: My snowman is *incomplete*, and one carrot nose will make him *complete*!

words.why: I-L joins LEGAL, so there are two L's.
words.def: Against the law or against the rules.
words.sent: It is illegal to park in front of a fire hydrant.
words.story: In soccer it is illegal for most players to touch the ball with their hands. Only the goalkeeper may!
words.card: It is *illegal* in my house to put your *leg* in the soup!

words.why: I-R joins REGULAR, so there are two R's.
words.def: Not even, or not following the usual pattern.
words.sent: The rock had a bumpy, irregular shape.
words.story: Most moons are round, but Mars has two small moons with lumpy, irregular shapes, a bit like potatoes!
words.card: A *regular* pancake is round, but mine is an *irregular* blob shaped like a duck!

words.why: I-M joins MATURE, so there are two M's.
words.sent: The immature apples were still small and green.
words.story: An immature frog is called a tadpole. At first it has gills, a tail, and no legs at all!
words.card: The *immature* green banana said, 'Wait! I will be *mature* and yellow by Tuesday!'

words.why: I-M joins PERFECT, because IN changes to IM before P.
words.def: Having a small mistake or flaw.
words.sent: My drawing was imperfect, but I loved it anyway.
words.story: In Japan, a cracked bowl may be mended with gold. The art is called kintsugi, and it makes the imperfect bowl even more beautiful!
words.card: My *imperfect* cookie had a bite missing, which made it *perfect* for sharing!

words.why: I-M joins PATIENT, because IN changes to IM before P.
words.sent: The impatient puppy pawed at the door.
words.story: Bamboo is a good plant for an impatient gardener: some kinds can grow almost a meter in a single day!
words.card: The *patient* turtle waited for the bus, but the *impatient* rabbit hopped on a skateboard!

words.why: I-L joins LOGICAL, so there are two L's.
words.sent: It would be illogical to wear a swimsuit in the snow.
words.story: Dreams are often illogical. In a dream you might fly or chat with a fish, and it all seems to make sense until you wake up!
words.card: It is *logical* to eat soup with a spoon and *illogical* to eat it with a comb!

words.why: I-R joins RESPONSIBLE, so there are two R's.
words.def: Not taking good care of the things you are trusted to do.
words.sent: It would be irresponsible to leave the garden gate open.
words.story: The cuckoo may seem irresponsible: it lays its egg in another bird's nest and lets that bird raise the chick!
words.card: A *responsible* pirate feeds the parrot, but an *irresponsible* pirate lets the parrot steer the ship!
